notes: Under A131 a crime victim decides whether to report from their own side: the harm of the offense against the trouble of reporting, how close they are to the offender (family at full strength, acquaintance sliding with shared moments), their own past reports and past charges, their temperament (reliability plus conflict) and their age. The weights are placeholders in UNRESEARCHED_REPORTING (src/simulation/crime/reporting.ts), set so a drawn town's totals sit near the 2022 NCVS shares reported: robbery 64.0 percent, assault 40.6 percent, burglary 44.9 percent.

The same NCVS table does not show that a close tie lowers reporting in raw totals. In 2022, 53.8 percent of domestic violence and 51.5 percent of intimate partner violence was reported against 36.0 percent of violence by strangers; in 2021 the figures were 48.9, 50.7 and 48.4 percent. Those totals mix severity, injury and repeat victimization with the tie itself, so they do not settle the tie's weight with other things held equal.
Vandalism has no share reported in the NCVS report checked; its harm weight is the smallest placeholder and is not checked against a total.
question: With the offense's seriousness held equal, how much does a victim's relationship to the offender, their earlier contact with police (as a reporter and as someone charged), their age and their temperament change the odds that they report a crime to police?

sourcesChecked.source: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Criminal Victimization, 2022, NCJ 307089, table 4
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Raw shares reported by offense and by victim-offender relationship; no model holding seriousness, injury or repeat victimization equal, and no figure for vandalism or for prior police contact.

title: Why crime victims report to police, or keep quiet
usableAnswer: Adjusted odds ratios (or shares with seriousness held equal) for reporting by victim-offender relationship, the victim's age, and the victim's earlier police contact, from a named NCVS analysis or comparable survey, so each placeholder weight can be read as data.
whyItMatters: Whether a crime reaches the police log decides what the local paper, the police and the prosecutor ever see, and a player who changes a town's ties or its police changes who reports.
